doc.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995

title: Lena Horne and Louie Bellson's help
summary: Opening with Ray Brown and Milt Jackson in Los Angeles, then Louie Bellson helped Duffy become Lena Horne's drummer at eighteen, touring with Alan King.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And within five hours after that I was on a flight to California. I packed my bags and dad put me on the plane and Ray Brown met me at the airport and drove me to the hotel and left me there, and like the next day I opened up with Teddy Edwards on sax, Milt Jackson, Ray Brown, Monty Alexander and myself. And for three weeks I was in a dream world like you would not believe, to play with these people. And right after that I got a phone call, now let me preface it, Louie Bellson has been a saint in my life. He helped me at the age of eighteen to become Lena Horne’s drummer. And this is after her husband had passed away, who was her conductor and husband for 45 years or so. And I played the first engagement with her that she came back, and we went on a year tour with Alan King all across the country. But the miraculous part is that around I’d say around eight weeks after I had graduated high school, I was back in Miami Beach playing as Lena Horne’s drummer with Alan King. And I got front row passes for all my teachers to come sit there and watch me play. I could barely read the music, I was making faces at all my teachers. But I had a ball, it was great. And you know it was wild because my father and
Lena were associated together in Charlie Barnet’s big band in the early 40s before my dad joined Woody Herman’s band. So Lena took extra special care of her little Chubby.
